subject: 1. USERS OF GPS RECEIVERS ARE ADVISED OF POTENTIAL PROBLEMS DUE TO
text:
1. USERS OF GPS RECEIVERS ARE ADVISED OF POTENTIAL PROBLEMS DUE TO
   GPS ROLL OVER. THIS PROBLEM IS RELATED TO THE FIRST ROLL OVER OF
   THE 1,024 WEEK GPS CLOCK CYCLE WHICH WILL OCCUR AT MIDNIGHT ON
   AUGUST 21, 1999.
2. ALL GPS RECEIVERS KEEP GPS TIME WHICH BEGAN ON JANUARY 6, 1980.
   GPS TIME IS INCLUDED AS A DATA FIELD IN THE NAVIGATIONAL MESSAGE
   TRANSMITTED BY EACH SATELLITE. SOME GPS RECEIVERS HAVE LIMITED
   STORAGE SPACE FOR THIS TIME INFORMATION AND CAN ONLY HOLD A
   MAXIMUM OF 1,023 WEEKS. THESE SYSTEMS WILL INTERPRET WEEK NUMBER
   1,024 AS 0.
3. MANY GPS RECEIVERS ARE KNOWN TO BE UNABLE TO MAKE THE TRANSITION
   FROM WEEK 1,023 TO 1,024. DURING THIS TIME THE INTERNAL CLOCKS OF
   THESE GPS RECEIVERS WILL EXPERIENCE A LACK OF ABSOLUTE REFERENCE
   AND MAY GIVE THE WRONG TIME AND POSITION OR MAY LOCK UP
   PERMANENTLY.
4. SOME OF THESE GPS RECEIVERS ARE REPAIRABLE WITH UPGRADES AND
   OTHERS WILL BECOME UNUSABLE. USERS ARE ADVISED TO CHECK WITH THEIR
   GPS MANUFACTURER REGARDING THE STATUS OF THEIR RECEIVER. CURRENTLY
   GPS RECEIVERS ARE IN THE 1,023RD WEEK.
5. FOR FURTHER INFORMATION SEE SECTION 2.3.5 (PAGES 18-19) OF THE GPS
   SPS SIGNAL SPECIFICATION, 2ND EDITION, ISSUED JUNE 2, 1995 WHICH
   REPEATS THE WORDS AND WARNINGS OF ICD-GPS-200. IN ADDITION GPS SPS
   SIGNAL SPECIFICATION MAY BE OBTAINED FROM THE WEB AS AN ADOBE
   ACROBAT (.PDF) DOCUMENT AT THE U.S. COAST GUARD'S SITE AT HTTP://
   WWW.NAVCEN.USCG.MIL/GPS/GENINFO/GPSDOCUMENTS/SIGSPEC/DEFAULT.HTM.
   REMEMBER, FAILURE TO CORRECT THE PROBLEM COULD LEAD TO SERIOUS
   NAVIGATIONAL PROBLEMS BY PLACING LIVES AND PROPERTY AT RISK.

subject: 1. THE U.S. COAST GUARD ADVISES DGPS AND LORAN USERS OF THE POTENTIAL
text:
1. THE U.S. COAST GUARD ADVISES DGPS AND LORAN USERS OF THE POTENTIAL
   FOR COMPUTER RELATED PROBLEMS DURING THE END-OF-FILE TRANSITION
   PERIOD (08 SEP 1999 - 09 SEP 1999). DURING THIS PERIOD, SOME
   COMPUTERS COULD EXPERIENCE DIFFICULTIES WHILE ATTEMPTING TO READ
   THE DATE 9/9/99. THIS IS BECAUSE SOME SOFTWARE PROGRAMS USE 9999
   TO DESIGNATE AN END-OF-FILE OR PROGRAM TERMINATION COMMAND.
2. THE U.S. COAST GUARD HAS TESTED THE DGPS AND LORAN SYSTEM
   COMPUTERS AND DO NOT ANTICIPATE PROBLEMS. HOWEVER, DISRUPTION OF
   SUPPORT SERVICES SUCH AS COMMERCIAL POWER, VOICE AND DATA
   COMMUNICATION NETWORKS, MANY OF WHICH THE U.S. COAST GUARD HAS
   LITTLE OR NO CONTROL OVER, COULD AFFECT THE AVAILABILITY OF DGPS
   AND LORAN. ALL USERS ARE URGED TO HAVE CONTINGENCY PLANS SHOULD
   THESE SYSTEMS BE AFFECTED.
3. IN ADDITION TO U.S. COAST GUARD RADIONAVIGATION SERVICES, USERS
   SHOULD BE AWARE THAT COMPUTER APPLICATIONS, SUCH AS ELECTRONIC
   CHARTING SYSTEMS, COULD ALSO BE AFFECTED.
4. QUESTIONS CONCERNING SPECIFIC COMPUTER APPLICATIONS SHOULD BE
   ADDRESSED DIRECTLY TO THE APPLICATIONS MANUFACTURER.
5. FOR FURTHER INFORMATION, PLEASE CONTACT THE U.S. COAST GUARD
   NAVIGATION CENTER AT (703) 313-5900 OR HTTP://WWW.NAVCEN.USCG.MIL.
6. CANCEL THIS MSG 10 SEP.

subject: 1.  IN PREPARATION FOR THE YEAR 2000 ROLLOVER, NUMEROUS TESTS HAVE
text:
1.  IN PREPARATION FOR THE YEAR 2000 ROLLOVER, NUMEROUS TESTS HAVE
    BEEN SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETED ON ALL SYSTEMS WITHIN THE MARINE
    NAVIGATION DEPARTMENT OF THE NATIONAL IMAGERY & MAPPING AGENCY.
    THESE SYSTEMS ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE PRODUCTION, MAINTENANCE
     AND DISSEMINATION OF MARITIME SAFETY INFORMATION. ALL SYSTEMS
    HAVE BEEN CERTIFIED TO BE Y2K COMPLIANT AND IT IS ANTICIPATED THAT
    THERE WILL BE NO INTERRUPTION IN OUR SERVICE AND OPERATIONS.
     CUSTOMERS SHOULD EXPECT NO DISRUPTION IN THE RECEIPT OF ANY
     OF OUR STANDARD HARDCOPY PRODUCTS TO INCLUDE THE US NOTICE TO
     MARINERS AND/OR THE PROMULGATION AND AVAILABILITY OF ANY OF
      OUR DATA ELECTRONICALLY VIA THE MARINE NAVIGATION DEPARTMENT
     WEBSITE, NAVIGATION INFORMATION NETWORK (NAVINFONET) AND THE
     WORLD-WIDE NAVIGATIONAL WARNINGS SERVICE (NAVAREA IV, NAVAREA XII,
     HYDROLANT AND HYDROPAC).
2. THE MARINE NAVIGATION DEPARTMENT HAS TAKEN MEASURES TO INSURE
   THAT CONTINGENCIES ARE IN PLACE THAT WILL ENABLE IMMEDIATE RESPONSE,
   SERVICE AND ACCESS TO VITAL MARITIME SAFETY INFORMATION. ADDITIONAL
   STAFFING WILL ALSO BE ON-SITE AROUND THE CLOCK THROUGHOUT THE 
   ROLLOVER WEEKEND TO ENSURE THAT ALL SYSTEMS REMAIN OPERATIONAL.
   A TELEPHONE NUMBER HAS BEEN ESTABLISHED TO RESPOND TO ANY
   QUESTIONS CONCERNING NIMA HYDROGRAPHIC PRODUCTS AND SERVICES AT
   1-800-362-6289 (1-800-DMA-NAVY).
3. AS A PRECAUTIONARY MEASURE, ALL NIMA NAVIGATION PUBLICATIONS THAT
   WERE PROGRAMMED TO BE PRINTED IN THE MONTH OF DECEMBER 1999 HAVE
   BEEN SENT TO PRINT CONTRACTORS AS OF 15 DECEMBER TO ALLOW FOR ALL
   PRINT QUANTITIES TO BE COMPLETED AND DELIVERED BY 31 DECEMBER 1999.
   IF THERE IS A Y2K PROBLEM EXTERNAL TO NIMA THAT IMPACTS THE PRINTING
   AND DISSEMINATION OF OUR PRODUCTS AFTER 01 JANUARY 2000, THE US 
   NOTICE TO MARINERS, LIST OF LIGHTS PUBLICATIONS, BROADCAST WARNINGS
   AND DAILY MEMORANDUMS WILL BE AVAILABLE VIA THE MARINE NAVIGATION
   DEPARTMENT WEBSITE AND NAVINFONET. THE WEBSITE CAN BE FOUND VIA THE
   NIMA HOMEPAGE (WWW.NIMA.MIL) UNDER THE MAPS & GEODATA ICON OR
   DIRECTLY AT HTTP://POLLUX.NSS.NIMA.MIL. CUSTOMERS MAY ALSO CORRESPOND
   DIRECTLY WITH THE MARINE NAVIGATION DEPARTMENT VIA E-MAIL ADDRESSED 
   TO NAVSAFETY@NIMA.MIL, THE WORLD-WIDE NAVIGATIONAL WARNING SERVICE
   BROADCAST WATCH DESK, PLA OF "NIMA NAVSAFETY BETHESDA MD" , OR BY
   USING THE TELEPHONE AND FAX NUMBERS FOUND LISTED IN THE INSIDE FRONT
   COVER OF THE WEEKLY US NOTICE TO MARINERS.
4. MARINERS ARE ENCOURAGED TO RELAY ANY Y2K RELATED MARITIME SAFETY 
   INFORMATION TO THIS OFFICE FOR EVALUATION AND ASSESSMENT FOR
   DISSEMINATION WORLDWIDE. IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT ALL VESSELS HAVE
   Y2K CONTINGENCY PLANS IN PLACE WHETHER THEY ARE AT SEA OR IN PORT
   DURING THIS PERIOD TO INSURE THEIR OPERATIONAL CAPABILITIES AND 
   SAFETY OF NAVIGATION. VESSELS SHOULD TAKE EXTRA PRECAUTION PRIOR TO 
   TAKING ARRIVAL TO INSURE THAT THE PORT IS OPEN TO TRAFFIC AND FULLY  
   OPERATIONAL.
